**2026-10-26.** A patch release with one fix: a message now reaches a process waiting at a
`<receiveTask>`. Everything in the v0.6.0 release notes applies. There is no `q:` namespace change
and no migration, and the snapshot format is unchanged, so an instance parked by a 0.6.0 engine
resumes under 0.6.1.

## Fixed: a receive task never received its message

A `<receiveTask>` parks the token until a correlated message arrives on one of its `<q:source>`
channels, the same park as an intermediate message catch event. Because it is an activity rather
than an event, it can also carry boundary events. That is how BPMN says "wait for this message, or
time out": attach an interrupting timer boundary. In a loop, it becomes a listen window that waits
for the next status, or gives up after N seconds.

The receive task parked correctly, but the message meant to resume it never arrived. When it came
in on the task's channel, the engine did not count the receive task among the nodes that can be
waiting for a message. It took the message for one that should start a process, found no start
event on that channel, and rejected it with `SUTRA.INBOUND.NO_START_EVENT_FOR_MESSAGE_TYPE` (HTTP
500). The parked instance stayed where it was, so with a timer boundary every window ran to its
timeout, and without one the instance waited forever.

In 0.6.1 a receive task is handled exactly like a message catch for that message:

- a `filterExpression` on its `<q:source>` and the channel's intake validation apply to it;
- correlation tries the task's own `<q:alias>` first, then the start event's
  `onConflict="correlate"` alias;
- the resume retires the task's timer boundary in the same step, and a loop that comes back to
  the task parks a new wait with a fresh timer;
- a message that matches no waiting instance is still refused with
  `SUTRA.RUNTIME.RELAY.CORRELATION_NOT_FOUND`, and the parked instance is left untouched.

An event-based gateway arm that is a receive task had the same defect and is fixed by the same
change. `sutra coverage init` now lists a `<q:send>` into a receive task's channel as a relay hop.

The fix has tests at two levels. In-process, against the dispatcher: a receive task correlated by
its own alias, and the listen window when a status arrives first, when the timer fires first, and
when an uncorrelated status arrives. In a container, against the engine image and PostgreSQL: the
same three listen-window cases, end to end over HTTP.

## Upgrading

Replace the image or the binary. Nothing in a deployment package needs to change.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.1
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.1
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.1"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.1"`.
